ABOUT COMPYL 

Compyl is an enterprise-grade Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform helping organizations automate risk management, compliance, and audit readiness across complex security environments. Based in NYC, our platform connects with hundreds of security tools to simplify evidence collection, streamline workflows, and give teams a more modern way to manage GRC at scale. We are building for speed, scale, and impact. Our culture is rooted in accountability, curiosity, and a strong bias toward execution. We value people who take ownership, move fast, and care deeply about building meaningful products that solve difficult problems.



THE ROLE 

As a Software Engineer, you will architect and build the heart of the Compyl platform. This team is responsible for our most critical feature set: an Agentic AI system that actively manages, remediates, and plans GRC workflows autonomously. You will not be building "bolt-on" AI chat features. You will be designing intelligent systems that take autonomous action within our robust C# / .NET and Blazor ecosystem. 



REQUIREMENTS 

 - C# / .NET Deep mastery of the .NET ecosystem, CQRS, and Onion Architecture (Controller → Service → Repository). You know how to design scalable systems that can handle complex state and AI orchestrations. 

 - Proven experience building agentic workflows, orchestrating LLMs to take action, parse structured data, and execute multi-step logic safely. 

 - Strong experience with Blazor WebAssembly/Server. You understand component-driven architecture, strict separation of logic (.razor.cs), and building highly interactive UIs. 

 - AI-Native Workflow Proficiency in Cursor, Claude Code, or Codex is mandatory. You leverage AI IDEs to automate boilerplate and write faster, cleaner code. 

 - You thrive in high-velocity environments, balancing rapid shipping with necessary architectural guardrails. 



HOW WE WORK 

At Compyl, engineering is expected to move with urgency while maintaining high standards for quality, performance, and security. We care about building systems the right way, but we also know how to make pragmatic decisions that keep the business moving. A few principles that guide our team: 

 - Frontend & API Rigor:  No inline styling — component-specific .scss only. Strict adherence to OpenAPI 3.1.1 standards with mandatory XML documentation for all public endpoints. 

 - The Campground Rule: We believe in leaving the codebase better than we found it. Engineers proactively address technical debt and clean up nullable warnings daily.

 - Accountability & Extreme Ownership: We ship code daily. While we have solid guardrails and automated testing (Playwright) in place, you are empowered to own your features from the IDE to production. 



WHY COMPYL 

Joining Compyl means working on meaningful technical challenges inside a growing SaaS company operating at the intersection of security, compliance, and automation. You'll have the chance to influence core architecture, work alongside a team that values execution, and help build the foundation for the next stage of our platform.

 - Opportunity to shape the growth and foundation of a high-impact SaaS product

 - A team that values collaboration, accountability, and transparency

Get to Know Us

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. 

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.



Summary

We're looking for a Senior/Staff Offensive Security Software Engineer with extensive web application penetration testing experience and a growing interest in AI-enhanced security techniques. You will have a significant impact on how we deliver value to our customers by designing, developing, and integrating web application penetration testing content into the NodeZero platform. This position requires practical expertise in full-scope web application testing, proven software development skills, and enthusiasm for leveraging emerging AI technologies to advance offensive security capabilities.



Essential Functions

 - Perform hands-on, full-scope web application penetration tests against real customer applications, alongside benchmark and lab targets, to surface vulnerabilities and attack paths.

 - Review NodeZero results on live customer engagements to identify coverage gaps, blind spots, and missed opportunities — the edge cases and corner-case attack scenarios that autonomous testing doesn't yet handle.

 - Manually reproduce and validate those edge cases, building reliable, production-safe proof-of-concept exploits and clear test cases that demonstrate the gap end to end — including against live customer environments without disrupting them.

 - Partner closely with software engineers to translate your findings into product improvements — defining detection logic, attack content, expected behavior, and remediation so NodeZero handles those cases going forward.

 - Build and maintain a library of regression and benchmark test cases so newly added coverage doesn't silently regress over time.

 - Monitor production pentests for missed findings and false positives; create and triage Jira tickets to drive issues to resolution.

 - Work directly with customers and internal teams to investigate findings, explain attack paths, and address questions about web application coverage and results.

 - Author technical blog posts and research write-ups showcasing new exploits, edge cases, and attack methodologies.

 - Mentor teammates and contribute to continuous improvement of team processes, methodology, and testing standards.
